The historical term names the Greek U-shaped letter plus -oid, not the later hyo- anatomical combining form. Greek hu letter upsilon + -oeidēs like, borrowing French/Latin; original source says U-shaped, whereas existing hyo combining form is hyoid bone, derived from the word itself. Do not map hyoid to a prefix formed from itself; propose hy U-shaped as independent historical form, with separate existing anatomical hyo bone sense.
Robust is an independently productive English adjective; robustly and robustness attach ordinary adverb and noun suffixes. Its ultimate Latin source is robustus, strong.

Webster identifies parthen- / partheno- as the same combining form and specifically gives parthenote; -ote is the ending. The source specifies prefix partheno-, while the published virgin-sense target is classed root. Record this as family lookup; the o may also be viewed as part of -ote.
Latin tellur- earth + -ian: inhabitant of earth / terrestrial.
Tellurium + chemical -ide: compound containing tellurium; historically element named from Latin earth, not all ground.
Tellurium + chemical -ite: tellurite mineral or oxyanion/salt; element itself is named from Latin earth.

garderobe belongs to the robe garment family, and French robe has documented Germanic booty/spoils ancestry shared with rob. The published root meaning includes spoils, permitting historical same-family retrieval. Do not teach the modern garment as robbery, or claim it derives from the English rob verb.

English rob means steal or plunder and is an independently productive base for robber and robbing. Robbery came via Old French roberie, an old French derivative of rober, so it shares the family without necessarily being created in English.
